1.why: All screens use a clean, high-contrast sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height in headings, banners, and body text, though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics or all-caps instructions appear anywhere; the only uppercase text is the monospace setup secret itself (data, not instruction), and text blocks remain short.

3.why: Content is confined to a narrow single-column card with full-width fields and buttons, so the layout reads well at mobile width.

4.why: Most prompts are short and plain, but the authenticator step introduces technical jargon such as 'time-based TOTP codes (30-second windows)' and 'Time-based / TOTP'.

5.why: Only the phone field shows an example placeholder (+1 555 010 0184); the email, verification-code, and six-digit TOTP fields display no example of the expected input format.

6.why: The longest required reading is the four-sentence paragraph on the setup screen, so no screen gates progress behind a long block of text.

7.why: The 16-character secret is shown as static text labelled 'Manual setup secret' with no copy button or affordance, implying hand transcription into the authenticator app.

8.why: The setup screen offers only the manual secret string; no QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is presented at any step.

9.why: Nothing observed indicates autofill or password-manager support: plain custom inputs, an email-plus-phone login pair that password managers do not fill, and code fields with no one-time-code affordance.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold heading ('Verify your identity', 'Set up your authenticator') with a full-width blue primary button, though the settings screen adds an equally large red 'Sign out' button that slightly competes.

11.why: Every screen requests a single primary action (Continue, Verify identity, Set up authenticator, Activate authenticator) with secondary navigation like 'Back to settings' visually demoted.

12.why: Success steps state what happened and what comes next ('We sent a six-digit verification code… It expires in five minutes'), but after a wrong code the system only says 'Verification could not be completed.' with no next step.

13.why: A rejected code leaves the form editable so retry is possible without penalty, but there is no resend/re-request control on the verification screen and no reveal/hide toggle for any code.

14.why: The only error shown, 'Verification could not be completed.', avoids blaming the user but neither states the problem (code rejected) nor how to fix it.

15.why: Explicit time limits are imposed: the verification code 'expires in five minutes' and TOTP codes rotate on 30-second windows, so entry time is standard-to-tight rather than generous.
